_meta.status: VERIFIED 2026-08-22. Every value below was checked against a primary source and the citation recorded in _meta.verification. These are population averages, not measurements of any individual.

conventions.units: All emission outputs are kg CO2e unless the key name says otherwise.
conventions.flights: NO radiative forcing multiplier is applied. DEFRA publishes both variants; we use the without-RF figures (0.074 / 0.069) rather than the with-RF figures (0.126 / 0.117). This understates the warming impact of flying by roughly 70%. Stated in the README so the number can be argued with.
conventions.meals: 14 main meals per week (lunch + dinner). Breakfast is not modelled. A meal factor is the protein component at a 100 g portion, not the whole plate.
conventions.ev: transportPerKm.evKwhPerKm is ENERGY, not emissions. The engine multiplies it by the province grid intensity at runtime, which is why an EV ranks differently in Quebec (1.9 g/kWh) than in Alberta (438 g/kWh).
conventions.gwp: Where CH4 and N2O were folded into a CO2e total, Schedule 3 (AR5) global warming potentials were used: CH4 = 28, N2O = 265.

foodPerMealKg.beefMeal.basis: 100 g portion x 99.48 kg CO2e/kg (beef herd) = 9.95
foodPerMealKg.beefMeal.source: Poore & Nemecek (2018), Science, via Our World in Data, Environmental impacts of food

foodPerMealKg.chickenMeal.source: Poore & Nemecek (2018), Science, via Our World in Data

foodPerMealKg.plantMeal.basis: 150 g pulses x 0.98 kg CO2e/kg = 0.15, plus grain and vegetable sides
foodPerMealKg.plantMeal.source: Poore & Nemecek (2018), Science, via Our World in Data

foodPerMealKg.cheeseHeavyMeal.source: Poore & Nemecek (2018), Science, via Our World in Data

transportPerKm.gasCar.source: UK DESNZ/DEFRA GHG Conversion Factors for Company Reporting 2025

transportPerKm.hybridCar.basis: Average hybrid car. CORRECTED from 0.11 placeholder.

transportPerKm.busPerPassenger.basis: Average local bus at average occupancy

transportPerKm.trainPerPassenger.basis: National rail. NOT currently used by the engine: both transit levers price replacement travel as bus, which emits about 3x more per passenger-km, so savings are understated rather than overstated. Retained deliberately, and the conservatism is stated in each transit lever assumptions string.

transportPerKm.evKwhPerKm.basis: Typical mid-size battery-electric vehicle, 20 kWh/100 km combined (55% city / 45% highway)
transportPerKm.evKwhPerKm.source: NRCan EnerGuide label for battery-electric vehicles

flightPerPassengerKm.shortHaul.basis: Short-haul economy, WITHOUT radiative forcing. CORRECTED from the 0.15 placeholder, which was a with-RF figure and roughly doubled the flight lever.

flightPerPassengerKm.longHaul.basis: Long-haul economy, WITHOUT radiative forcing. CORRECTED from the 0.19 placeholder.

flightPerPassengerKm.shortHaulTripKm.basis: 1250 km each way. Representative Canadian short-haul: Toronto-Halifax is ~1300 km each way, Toronto-Chicago ~700. The DEFRA short-haul band is under 3700 km one-way. CORRECTED from 1500 round trip, which was only 750 km each way.
flightPerPassengerKm.shortHaulTripKm.source: Assumption, sanity-checked against real routes. Not a measurement.

flightPerPassengerKm.longHaulTripKm.basis: 5500 km each way. Toronto-London is ~5700 km each way. CORRECTED from 8000 round trip, which is Toronto-Los Angeles, not an intercontinental trip.
flightPerPassengerKm.longHaulTripKm.source: Assumption, sanity-checked against real routes. Not a measurement.

homeEnergy.gasKgPerM3.basis: Ontario marketable natural gas 1921 g CO2/m3, plus residential CH4 0.037 g x 28 and N2O 0.035 g x 265, giving 1931 g CO2e/m3. Provincial spread is narrow (1915-1966 g CO2/m3).
homeEnergy.gasKgPerM3.source: ECCC, Emission factors and reference values v3.0 (October 2025), Tables 1.3 and 2.3

homeEnergy.avgAnnualHeatingM3.basis: Average residential natural gas customer, 2024. Covers all household gas use, not space heating alone. National range is 1500-3100.
homeEnergy.avgAnnualHeatingM3.source: Canadian Gas Association, Natural Gas Facts

homeEnergy.oilKgPerLitre.basis: Light Fuel Oil - Residential 2753 g CO2/L, plus CH4 0.026 g x 28 and N2O 0.006 g x 265, giving 2755 g CO2e/L.
homeEnergy.oilKgPerLitre.source: ECCC, Emission factors and reference values v3.0 (October 2025), Table 4.3

homeEnergy.avgAnnualHeatingLitres.basis: Canadian home heating with oil, per heating season. Atlantic Canada runs up to 1500. CORRECTED from the 1500 placeholder to the national average.
homeEnergy.avgAnnualHeatingLitres.source: Canadian heating oil distributor consumption data, consistent with NRCan Survey of Household Energy Use

homeEnergy.thermostatSetbackSavingsPct.basis: 2 degree setback held over an 8-hour period. CORRECTED from the 0.12 placeholder, which overstated what a 2 degree setback achieves.
homeEnergy.thermostatSetbackSavingsPct.source: Metered thermostat setback study data, consistent with NRCan and US DOE setback guidance

homeEnergy.avgAnnualHeatingKwhElectric.basis: Space heating only, for a dwelling whose primary heat is electric. Distinct from the 11135 kWh average total household electricity figure, which covers all end uses across all heating types.
homeEnergy.avgAnnualHeatingKwhElectric.source: NRCan Survey of Household Energy Use 2019, residential sector energy intensity

gridGPerKwh.*.basis: Consumption intensity as delivered to the consumer, Table 5.3, the table applicable to calendar year 2026. Notable corrections from placeholders: PE 20 to 234 (PEI imports from New Brunswick and is not near-zero), NS 300 to 581, NT 180 to 420, ON 30 to 59, SK 580 to 631.
gridGPerKwh.*.source: ECCC, Emission factors and reference values v3.0 (October 2025), Table 5.3, aligned with National Inventory Report 1990-2023
